doc.title: Bernard Purdie interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003

title: Doing the job plus a touch of Purdie; refusing to bad-mouth
summary: He recalls telling Barry Manilow he is not Steve Gadd, lists artists he loves and refuses to talk badly about Aretha.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Exactly. You want Steve, you call him. I’ll be glad to call him for you. But you know when I was coming along I didn’t know that that’s the way it was. You had to play like somebody else in order to do that. Well I didn’t. I played me. But I played and did the job. Now I was fortunate enough to have enough in me to do the job plus. That’s what I’ve done all my life. Do the job plus stick a little bit of me in. And that’s how I’ve done over all these years. I’m going to go in and I’m going to do the job. I’m going to play the music and then I’m going to add a touch of Purdie. Now I thought that’s what you called me for. And after all these years I’m still doing the same thing. I’m still doing the job. But I thought you wanted a little bit of me. And that’s how I do it. So if that means that I’m still arrogant, fine, I’m still arrogant. The point is that I’m there to do the job. I will always love Aretha, the Rolling Stones, Hall & Oates, Steely Dan. I’m always going to love them — B.B. King — like a father to me. job and I said yes I can do it. That’s what I’m going to do. But I get along with everybody and no matter who it is. Cissy, Whitney, it doesn’t matter. That to me is part of life. That’s why I’m in the position that I’m in, that’s why I like everybody, that’s why I can talk about everybody. But I always have something positive to say. Now I could go and I could have made a million dollars instead if I’d have talked about all the bad things about Aretha while I was there. For what? Then I’d never work.
You wouldn’t feel good about yourself either.
Not only that but nobody would hire me to play.
I says no, no, no, no, no, no, no, no, no. Money? I can still earn a good living. So no, no, no. Can’t go that route.
